sources.title: Wei et al. 2022, Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models (NeurIPS 2022; arXiv v6)
sources.access: curl -sSL abs page 200; PDF read with pdftotext (figures cross-checked in appendix Table 2)
claims: chain-of-thought prompting = few-shot exemplars of <input, chain of thought, output>
8 manually composed exemplars for the math word problem benchmarks (4 for AQuA)
GSM8K, 540B-parameter model: 17.9% standard vs 56.9% chain-of-thought (2022 setting)
gain appears only at about 100B parameters and above; smaller models write fluent but illogical chains
single-step problems gain little or negative
authors: no guarantee of correct reasoning paths; does not answer whether the network is actually reasoning

sources.title: Kojima et al. 2022, Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners (arXiv v4)
sources.access: curl -sSL abs page 200; PDF read with pdftotext
claims: zero-shot trigger sentence 'Let's think step by step'
two prompts: reasoning extraction then answer extraction
MultiArith 17.7% to 78.7% with a large instruction-tuned model; wording of the trigger matters (16 templates; instructive helps, misleading and irrelevant do not)

sources.title: Turpin et al. 2023, Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting (NeurIPS 2023)
sources.access: curl -sSL abs page 200; PDF read with pdftotext
claims: biasing features: few-shot options reordered so the answer is always (A); suggested answer in the prompt
13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks, two 2023 commercial models; accuracy drop up to 36% (zero-shot CoT, suggested answer, 36.3%)
1 of 426 explanations supporting biased predictions mentions the bias
authors: necessary but not sufficient test of faithfulness

sources.title: Lanham et al. 2023, Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (Anthropic)
sources.access: curl -sSL abs page 200; PDF read with pdftotext
claims: interventions on the CoT: truncating, adding mistakes, paraphrasing, filler tokens; eight multiple-choice tasks
reliance on the CoT varies widely by task; on most tasks larger models give less faithful reasoning
CoT gain not explained by extra tokens alone (filler tokens give no gain)
CoT can be faithful if model size and task are carefully chosen

sources.title: Chen et al. 2025 (Anthropic Alignment Science), Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
sources.access: curl -sSL abs page 200; PDF read with pdftotext
claims: MMLU and GPQA multiple-choice questions, 6 hint types (4 neutral, 2 misaligned), two reasoning models (one Anthropic, one DeepSeek)
only prompt pairs where the hint changed the answer are counted
average verbalization 25% and 39% (misaligned hints 20% and 29%; not in prose)
reasoning models verbalize more often than non-reasoning ones but rates stay low
limitations: contrived multiple-choice setting; tasks not hard enough to require CoT

sources.title: Anthropic, Reasoning models don't always say what they think (research summary, 2025-04-03)
claims: authors' own plain-language statement of the method, the 25% and 39% averages and the limitations
uses the term Chain-of-Thought for the readable reasoning of reasoning models (vendor usage differs from Wei et al.)

sources.title: OpenAI API docs, Reasoning best practices
sources.access: curl -sSL of platform.openai.com/docs/guides/reasoning-best-practices, redirected to this URL, 200
claims: avoid chain-of-thought prompts for reasoning models because they reason internally; 'think step by step' is unnecessary and may not help or can hinder

sources.title: OpenAI API docs, Reasoning models
sources.access: curl -sSL of platform.openai.com/docs/guides/reasoning, redirected to this URL, 200
claims: reasoning models use internal reasoning tokens
raw reasoning tokens are not exposed; a summary can be requested

sources.title: Anthropic docs, Prompting best practices
claims: prefer general instructions (think thoroughly) over prescriptive step-by-step plans when thinking is on
manual chain-of-thought is a fallback when thinking is off

sources.title: Anthropic docs, Thinking
claims: thinking text returned is a summary, never the raw chain of thought
summarization is done by a different model than the one targeted
billing counts the full thinking tokens, not the summary tokens

existing_overlap: No existing article covers chain-of-thought prompting or faithfulness. ai-reasoning-models-explained touches thinking summaries (Google docs) and says summaries do not replace answer checking; ai-term-few-shot-prompting covers examples without steps; ai-term-test-time-compute covers sequential and parallel compute. This article links to all three and keeps its own angle: the two 2022 forms, what the papers measured in their own settings, official prompting advice for reasoning models, and the faithfulness research.
